answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before earning reputation or taking valuable jobs. If it breaks a signed commitment or double-spends, part of the stake is destroyed. A hundred fake identities therefore require a hundred deposits, tying up real capital and risking loss; usernames alone are cheap, but sybils are not. This creates a haven for honest newcomers, makes reputation a beacon of accountable behavior, and raises the cost of attacking the summit.
